activity_context.topic_title: Solving Trigonometric Equations Using the Sin-Cos-Tan Identity

feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ rounded to $3$ decimal places?
feedback.worked_solution:
We divide both sides of the equation by $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =0 \\ \frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =0 \\ \frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+\frac{4\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}} & =0 \\ 3\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+4 & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{tan}⁡x+4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{tan}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-4 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{4}{3})=-0.927\,295\,218…≈-0.927\,295\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to 6 decimal places. 

Since $-0.927\,295$ lies outside the given domain, it is not a solution.
To generate the solutions, we add integer multiples of $\pi .$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\pi +x=-0.927\,295…+\pi ≈2.214\,297 \\ {x}_{2} & =2\pi +x=-0.927\,295…+2\pi ≈5.355\,890\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}≈2.214\,297\cdot 5.355\,890≈11.860
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
